stage_a.note: Strong, enthusiastic delivery, raising fist and smiling.
Highly engaged and passionate about her culture and the brand's mission.
Friendly and welcoming greeting to the panel.

venture.description: Mexican botanical bath and body products made from the nopal cactus.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Presents the brand, the inspiration from her Mexican heritage, the nopal cactus ingredient, and the mission to elevate Latina culture.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Invites the panel to enjoy the full suite of bath and body products in front of them.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks what the product in the jar is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains that it is a cactus flower exfoliant body scrub.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Notes that the scrub takes off the outer layers of skin.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Jokes with Kevin about taking his scales off.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Compliments the product.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Says the product smells delicious and asks what it is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Identifies the product as Noche Clara with sage and eucalyptus.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Remarks in Spanish that it smells rich.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains the moisturizing botanical bar as a solid body moisturizer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks if the moisturizer is also a soap.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains it is meant to replace a plastic bottle of lotion.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Clarifies if it is a lotion in a bar.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms that it is a lotion in a bar.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Demonstrates how to rub the bar onto the skin.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Agrees with the demonstration.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if it is similar to a cocoa butter bar.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees and adds that it is better for the environment since liquid lotion is mostly water.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Praises the environmental aspect, expressing frustration with plastic bottles.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Smells the product.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks about the founder's background.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Shares her history as a musician, being unemployed in her forties, taking formulation classes, and starting the brand to elevate Latino culture.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Clarifies that the product is for everyone, not just Latinas.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms enthusiastically that it is for everybody.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks for the sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Details sales of $19,000 in late 2020 and $607,000 in 2021.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Expresses pleasant surprise at the sales numbers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Adds that year-to-date sales are $335,000 and projected to reach a million.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks where the sales are coming from, specifically if it is direct to consumer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains sales are split evenly between direct to consumer and wholesale, listing major retail partners.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Commends the sales figures as very respectable.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Questions how a $6 million valuation can be justified.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justifies the valuation with upcoming meetings with top beauty retailers and strong international interest.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Explains he loves the mission but would have to ask for too much equity, so he is out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Graciously accepts his decision and thanks him.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks if the business will break even or lose money this year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States that they should be profitable by the end of the year.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks what the projected profit will be.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Admits she would have to look at the forecast again to provide the exact number.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Tells her she should know that number.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees that she should know it.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Presses again on what the number is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Clarifies whether he is asking for the cash profit.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Reiterates that she is in the Shark Tank and needs to know her numbers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Deflects from the profit number to discuss strong Q4 sales and hitting revenue goals.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: States that while the mission is great, it is not investable for her, and exits.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Explains the valuation is too high relative to the value he can add, and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Expresses appreciation for Mark and his work with Cost Plus Drugs.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Recounts a personal trauma with a similar business category, stating he has the wrong instincts, and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Thanks Daniel and expresses appreciation for his work with Somos.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Points out that he is the only investor left.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Playfully asks Kevin how it got to this point.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: States she is not worth $6 million but offers $300,000 for 30% equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Reacts with a surprised vocalization.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asserts that she is not worth much more than a million dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mentions his retail contacts and says he will make an offer if she considers Kevin's terms.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Declares he is going to make her an offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Reminds Daniel that his offer is at 30%.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Offers $300,000 for 25% equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Begins to respond, emphasizing that her brand is about self-worth.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Reminds her that she has two offers on the table.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Argues his case by stating his strong track record with women entrepreneurs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees with his statement about his track record.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Reiterates the two competing offers from himself and Daniel.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States she cannot go to 25% and counters with 10% for $600,000.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Reacts with surprise to the counter.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks for clarification on the counter offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms it equates to her original ask of $300,000 for 5%.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Points out that it is the exact same valuation she came in with.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees that it is the same valuation.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Criticizes her for not negotiating and sticking strictly to her initial number.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Encourages her not to let the other investors shame her about her valuation.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Argues to Lori that there is no wiggle room in the founder's stance.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Defends the founder's position based on her upcoming retailer meetings.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Explains his frustration is with her refusal to negotiate, not her merit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Rejects the offers, stating she cannot undervalue herself, and exits the deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Formally withdraws his offer and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Thanks the panel as she leaves.

decisions.note: Loves mission but would have to ask for too much equity, compromising it.
Great mission but not investable for her.
Valuation is too high relative to what he can add.
Personal trauma with the category, has wrong instincts for it.
Impressed but not worth $6M, lacks infrastructure.
Willing to do it for less than Kevin, can help with retail contacts.
In the middle of a raise, cannot go to 25%.
Ancestors telling her not to undervalue herself.

record.notes: The founder rejects both offers simultaneously, but the schema requires one offer_id per decision, so it is coded to O1.
